first_impression.reaction: Googled 'getting married in hawaii' because my fiancee has it on the shortlist and I want to know if the legal side is a trap. The intro gives me the answer in three steps with a 30-day rule. No 'paradise awaits'. Jumped to the FAQ first like I always do. Most answers are straight and point to the actual Hawaii government pages, which I can check myself. Two things bug me. The witness question gets a non-answer. And the page twice says 'pay the required fee' or 'a fee applies' without a number. I'm a finance guy, give me the number or tell me where it lives. The Wedded Wonderland bits are kept to the end and mostly low-key, but they make a couple of claims they don't back up.

journey.quote: There is no residency requirement, no US citizenship requirement and no blood test.
journey.reaction: That's the stuff I actually wanted to know, in one line. Good.

journey.quote: Ask your officiant what the ceremony itself requires on the day, including witnesses, and how the marriage is registered afterwards.
journey.reaction: The heading is 'Do you need witnesses?' and the answer is 'ask someone else'. That's the one FAQ that ducks. Either you know or you don't. If you don't, don't put it up as a question you're answering.

journey.quote: In most cases, yes. An overseas marriage is legally recognised in Australia if it was valid where it took place and would have been valid under Australian law.
journey.reaction: 'In most cases' plus the actual test. Hedged properly, not oversold. I'd check it on Smartraveller, and they've linked it.

journey.section: Can Australians marry legally in Hawaii?
journey.quote: As at November 2026, to marry lawfully in Hawaii you need a marriage licence issued by an authorised agent of the Hawaii State Department of Health.
journey.reaction: A date and a named authority. That's what I want on a legal page.

journey.quote: Couples who choose it usually marry legally at home, then travel for the celebration with every logistical question answered in advance.
journey.reaction: 'Every logistical question answered in advance'? By whom? That's a sales line slipped into the legal bit. Small, but I noticed.

journey.section: Before you go: entry and documents
journey.quote: An approved ESTA or valid visa does not guarantee entry.
journey.reaction: Telling me the catch up front. That's the tone I trust.

journey.quote: Complete the online marriage licence application at emrs.ehawaii.gov and pay the required fee.
journey.reaction: How much? It's a state fee, it's public. I don't need it to the cent, but 'the required fee' with no figure and no link to where the figure lives feels like a gap on a page this detailed.

journey.section: Pick up your licence together, in person
journey.quote: You must appear together, in person. Proxies are not allowed.
journey.reaction: Clear and practical. The bit about the appointment waiting for the second flight is the kind of real-world detail that tells me someone thought it through.

journey.quote: If you book a local officiant, ask to see their current State of Hawaii performer licence before you pay a deposit.
journey.reaction: Advice that protects me before I hand over money. After my last vendor, this is exactly the check I'd want someone to remind me of.

journey.quote: Processing usually takes up to four to six weeks, and delays can occur.
journey.reaction: A number and an honest caveat. Same section says 'a fee applies' though, again with no amount.

journey.section: Getting your certificate ready for Australia
journey.quote: It may not work as proof of a name change, so check with your state or territory registry of births, deaths and marriages first.
journey.reaction: That's a real catch most sites would skip. Points for saying it.

journey.section: Registering or recognising your marriage at home
journey.quote: Many couples do exactly that, with a long lunch at home for the guests who could not fly.
journey.reaction: 'Many couples' based on what? Harmless, but it's an unsupported generalisation on an otherwise sourced page.

journey.section: Permits for beach and outdoor ceremonies
journey.quote: The applicant submits a Certificate of Liability Insurance with the application, and the ceremony must follow DLNR's General Terms and Conditions for Commercial Activity.
journey.reaction: Useful. But who is 'the applicant' in practice: us, the officiant, the planner? And who pays for the insurance? That's where hidden costs live.

journey.quote: If you are weighing two islands against your guest list, Wedded Concierge can help you compare them on your dates.
journey.reaction: First sales nudge, but it comes after a lot of evidence and it's one line. I can live with it.

journey.quote: Everything else, from the lawn to the last shuttle, is a planning decision, and it is where a Hawaii wedding becomes yours.
A Wedded Advisor plans your venue, travel, vendors and payments as one point of contact from start to finish, and confirms inclusions in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: Inclusions in writing is the right promise. 'Plans your payments' is where I'd ask whether they take a cut from the venue. Nothing here tells me, and there's no real Hawaii wedding shown to back the claim.

Do you have anyone on the ground in Hawaii, or is it all run from Australia? (deferred business detail)

turn_offs_found.quote: Couples who choose it usually marry legally at home, then travel for the celebration with every logistical question answered in advance.
turn_offs_found.why: Absolute marketing claim ('every logistical question') tucked into a legal explanation, with no evidence and no clear subject. It's the kind of line that makes me wonder what else is spin.

turn_offs_found.quote: Many couples do exactly that, with a long lunch at home for the guests who could not fly.
turn_offs_found.why: Unsupported 'many couples' generalisation on a page that otherwise backs everything with a source.

turn_offs_found.quote: Ask your officiant what the ceremony itself requires on the day, including witnesses, and how the marriage is registered afterwards.
turn_offs_found.why: The FAQ heading promises an answer and this sentence passes the buck. It's the one place the page looks like it's dodging.

would_share_with: My fiancee, the 'What to bring' list and the two 30-day rules, for our trip planning spreadsheet
Our Reddit thread, the line about checking the officiant's performer licence before paying a deposit, and the name-change caveat on the certificate

cta_reaction.quote: Your Wedded Advisor works in your time zone, quotes in AUD, and agrees the fee in writing before any work begins.
cta_reaction.why: It comes after the evidence, not before, and it's concrete: AUD quotes and the fee in writing are the right promises. But my main questions, how the fee is worked out and whether they take a cut from Hawaii suppliers, aren't answered. The legal guide earns them a look, not a call. I'd email those questions before booking anything.

top_3_changes: Fix the witnesses FAQ: give a sourced yes/no answer if the source pack supports one, or reword the heading so it doesn't promise an answer the page can't give (e.g. 'Who needs to be at the ceremony?').

Where the page says 'pay the required fee' and 'a fee applies', either state the current amount with a source and date (flagged for checking), or say plainly that the Department publishes the current fee and link the exact page beside the sentence.

Cut or soften the two unsupported lines: drop 'with every logistical question answered in advance' from the symbolic ceremony paragraph, and change 'Many couples do exactly that' to something that doesn't claim a number (e.g. 'Some couples follow it with a long lunch at home').

open_questions.question: Does the source pack contain the current Hawaii licence and certified-copy fees and any witness requirement? If yes, the two medium objections can be closed with sourced lines; if not, the reworded heading and a direct fee-page link are the fallback.

assumptions: Daniel arrived via Google for 'getting married in hawaii' while Hawaii is on the shortlist and he is comparing planners; relevance is 4 because the legal content is exactly what he wanted, and enquiry likelihood is 2 because his fee and commission questions about Wedded Wonderland stay open.
Business details (fees, commissions, ground team, real weddings, scale, perks, Privileges, transfers, paperwork help) are deferred by the brief; voiced as unanswered questions only.
Rendered link text was quoted without markdown link syntax, as a reader would see it.
The 3-minute budget covered the intro, FAQ, licence steps, officiant, certificate and Australia sections, and the Wedded Wonderland sections, with a skim of the climate and island sections.
